materialDissent: Dissent from the packet's framing that round 17 'closes the last methodology gap.' The corrected alias search does close round 16's specific finding about exit-code consumers, but the packet's consumer analysis is scoped exclusively to *exit-code* consumers. This diff also changes a second observable contract: the persisted audit `reason` string. Cases that previously wrote `marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum` (unparseable timestamp, and — via the old `age < 0` fall-through — future-dated timestamp) now write the newly introduced `marker-age-unmeasurable`. Opus raised this in round 16 and it was classified as 'same class of residual as the exit-code question, disclosed identically' — but that classification is not accurate: unlike the out-of-repo exit-code question, the audit-reason string IS observable by an in-repo grep, and no such grep appears anywhere in this packet. It is a cheaper, in-scope check that was categorized into the unobservable-residual bucket rather than performed.

Dissent from treating the exit-2/exit-20 partition as fully test-covered. Both `JIRA_QUEUE.md` and the in-script `--help` text explicitly enumerate `submit`'s separate retry-verification-interval wait as a case that *remains* exit 2 — that is a load-bearing distinguishing claim in user-facing documentation. The added tests cover poll exhaustion, search failure, unmeasurable marker age, future-dated markers, and the discard/unfreeze index-lag paths, but no added test exercises the submit retry-verification path and asserts EXIT.STATE_ERROR. review.recommendation: Approve the design and the diff as written; do not gate another round on production-code changes. The change is structurally sound and strictly fail-safe: every path that previously blocked still blocks, `youngestMarkerAgeMs` returning `null` instead of `0`/negative for unmeasurable ages cannot produce a false `verify-clear` (both call sites use direct comparison, confirmed by the three-match call-site inventory), the nested ternary in `gateExitCode` has correct precedence, `Infinity` for the empty-marker case still short-circuits correctly, and 20 remains nonzero so any generic `code !== 0` handling — in or out of repo — is unaffected. Exit-inventory collision and the retired 10-12 range are both asserted by test. Before merge, run two cheap in-repo checks and record the output rather than reasoning about them: (1) `rg -n --hidden --no-ignore -g '!**/.git/**' -g '!**/node_modules/**' 'marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum|marker-age-unmeasurable|index-lag|search-unavailable'` and confirm every live match is inside the four changed files — this closes the audit-reason contract the same way the alias search closed the exit-code contract; (2) `rg -n 'entry\.reason|\.reason\s*===|\.reason\s*==' plugins/kstack/scripts/kstack-jira.mjs` to confirm no code branches on a persisted audit `reason` value, which is the backward-compatibility question for draft files already on disk carrying the old string. Separately, consider adding one regression test asserting `submit`'s retry-verification-interval wait still exits 2, since that partition is stated explicitly in two user-facing docs but is not asserted anywhere. One maintainability note for a follow-up, not this change: `preMutationDuplicateGate`'s returned `reason` field and the audit record's `reason` field draw from the same `VERIFICATION_REASON` enum but carry different semantics — `INDEX_LAG` is only ever an exit-code routing token and is never written to any audit record, while `MARKER_YOUNGER_THAN_INDEX_LAG_MINIMUM` is only ever an audit value and never routes an exit code. A future contributor adding a gate path can plausibly set the audit-facing constant on the return value and silently get exit 2 where 20 was intended. Separate field names (e.g. `exitReason` vs `auditReason`) would make that class of mistake impossible.
review.strongestObjection: The packet declares the consumer investigation complete on the strength of an exit-code search, but this diff changes two observable contracts, not one. The persisted audit `reason` string silently changes for the unparseable-timestamp case and for the future-dated-timestamp case (which previously fell through the old `Number.isFinite(age) ? age : 0` branch as a negative number and was labeled `marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum`), and both now emit the brand-new `marker-age-unmeasurable`. Seventeen rounds of increasingly rigorous grep methodology were spent on exit-code consumers while this second contract was classified as an unobservable out-of-repo residual — which it is not: it is greppable in-repo in one command, and no such grep appears anywhere in the packet. The identical failure shape that produced round 16's finding (an evidence category asserted rather than executed) therefore recurs here in a different category, even though round 16's specific instance is genuinely fixed.
